about: Every file in this repository that can reach the network, start a process, use the clipboard, the Windows registry, or global input, read other applications' text, write files, use browser storage, or load code or pickled data, with the reason; and every Rust file's count of `unsafe`. security/check_capabilities.py fails when the source and this file disagree.

engine.summary: The inference engine (litmus-engine), file reading and the reading cache (litmus-files), the `litmus` command line (litmus-cli), and the Python module litmus_engine (litmus-py), which reads a release's three files and writes none. No network code. `engine/litmus-py/build_wheel.sh` builds the Linux wheel by `docker run`, which the scan's shell patterns do not see: it pulls maturin's image, and the container downloads the pinned Rust and the locked crates, writing only the wheel to the folder it is given. `litmus mcp` (litmus-cli) serves the Model Context Protocol on standard input and output: it reads the texts and the one file path an agent sends, writes nothing, keeps no cache, and uses no network; a PDF is read through the same child process as `litmus score`.

app.summary: The desktop and browser app (egui). No network code except the contribute feature's browser build, which the published page does not use.

site.summary: The static site and the browser page's host page and worker, which load the page's own files and the model's three files from the page's own address.

contribute.summary: The contribute site's server, written and not deployed: the one place a checked text is sent and stored.

training.summary: Corpus building, training, evaluation, and the vendored foundry library they import. Runs on the trainer's machine in Docker; downloads datasets and models from the Hugging Face Hub and logs to Weights and Biases.

demo.summary: The advertisement and its teaser, rendered with Node from code, real captures of the app and the site, and measured numbers; never shipped. Its tools run the `litmus` command line, ffmpeg and headless Chromium, download public-domain documents, and record the Linux app on a virtual display in Docker on a machine the user names.

verification.summary: The checks in this file's family and the build and model verifiers.

release.summary: The release build and the release driver (`release/cut.py`, `release/litmus_release/`): the shipped programs, site, and contribute page built from the source and a trained release folder, and the staged commands that fetch, measure, fill the documents, build, and publish a release. The build has no network, except `release/build_linux.sh`, which the scan's shell patterns do not see: it runs the Linux build by `docker run` of maturin's pinned manylinux2014 image, whose container downloads the pinned Rust and the locked crates and writes only to the output folder it is given. The driver reads the model repository and the stored baseline scores from the Hugging Face Hub, and sends to the Hub, GitHub, and Pages only in a stage run with `--confirm`.

workflows.summary: `release-build.yml`, which the scan does not read: run by hand or on a published release, never on a push or pull request, with read-only repository access and no secrets. On GitHub's runners it downloads the release's model files from a URL, pinned Python packages, the pinned Rust, the locked crates, and maturin's pinned image; builds and tests on macOS, Linux, and Windows; and keeps the programs as the run's artifacts. It publishes nothing.

agents.summary: The Litmus agent skill (`.agents/skills/litmus`), its install scripts, and the Claude Code plugin and MCP registration files that point at it. The scripts download one program and the release's file list from github.com/lhallee/litmus releases, check the program against the list, and write only the program; nothing else here reaches the network.

app/src/quick/windows.rs.reason: the Win32 calls of quick check: COM and UI Automation, the clipboard, SendInput, the registry entry, all behind Settings

app/src/window_place.rs.reason: two Win32 calls, GetDpiForSystem and MonitorFromPoint, to restore the window on a screen that exists

app/tests/quick_windows.rs.reason: the Windows quick-check test's own Win32 calls on its scratch registry key and the clipboard

app/tests/release.rs.reason: std::env::set_var in a test, which Rust 2024 marks unsafe

engine/litmus-cli/src/memory.rs.reason: a counting global allocator for `litmus bench`'s peak memory, forwarding every call to the system allocator

engine/litmus-cli/src/strip.rs.reason: three Win32 console calls that turn on color escapes for this process's own standard output

engine/litmus-engine/examples/wasm_probe.reason: a WebAssembly test module that passes raw pointers to JavaScript for timing; not part of any release

engine/litmus-engine/src/codes.rs.reason: AVX2 intrinsics for the integer dot products of the int8 compare, called only after a runtime CPU check; the portable loops give the same integers

engine/litmus-engine/src/dense.rs.reason: AVX2 intrinsics for the float64 products, called only after a runtime CPU check; the scalar path gives the same bits

engine/litmus-engine/src/dense_neon.rs.reason: NEON intrinsics for the float64 products; the scalar path gives the same bits

engine/litmus-engine/src/dense_simd128.r.reason: WebAssembly SIMD128 intrinsics for the float64 products; the scalar path gives the same bits

engine/litmus-engine/src/integer_attenti.reason: SIMD intrinsics for integer attention on each backend, tested equal to the portable path

engine/litmus-engine/src/kernels/avx2.rs.reason: AVX2 intrinsics of the ternary kernels, called only after a runtime CPU check

engine/litmus-engine/src/kernels/mod.rs.reason: the calls into each backend's intrinsics, made only for a backend the CPU check selected

engine/litmus-engine/src/kernels/neon.rs.reason: NEON intrinsics of the ternary kernels

engine/litmus-engine/src/kernels/simd128.reason: WebAssembly SIMD128 intrinsics of the ternary kernels
